metadata.proof: SOURCE: Settings.py 'Security hardening' block configures SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE, X_FRAME_OPTIONS, SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY — but OMITS SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT (defaults to False) and SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS (defaults to 0 / no HSTS). Session and CSRF cookies have SECURE=True (not DEBUG), so they are not sent over HTTP — causing all authenticated requests to fail or silently downgrade. Without HSTS, a man-in-the-middle can trivially strip HTTPS on the first visit (sslstrip attack) and capture session tokens in plaintext. All form data (passwords, case details) are sent in cleartext.

The database is PostgreSQL by default (port 5432), accessible from any host reaching the network.
